content.title: A Guide to DC’s Cherry Blossoms: History, Hidden Gems & Must-See Spots | The Dupont Circle
content.text: Monday, 23, March 2026 Filed under: The Dupont Circle From the storied past of Washington’s iconic trees to the best places to experience peak bloom, here’s everything you need to know for the perfect spring outing. Springtime in Washington, DC, is synonymous with the breathtaking bloom of the cherry blossoms, attracting visitors from around the world. While iconic spots like the Tidal Basin are renowned for their beauty, the city offers numerous other hidden gem locations to experience the trees in their full glory. The cherry blossoms in Washington, DC, are more than just a beautiful spectacle; they symbolize a lasting friendship between the United States and Japan. The journey of these iconic trees to the nation's capital began in the late 19th century. In 1885, Eliza Ruhamah Scidmore, after returning from Japan, proposed planting Japanese cherry trees along the Potomac River waterfront. Despite her persistent efforts over 24 years, her idea didn't gain immediate traction. Simultaneously, botanist David Fairchild imported 1,000 cherry trees from Japan in 1906, planting them on his property in Chevy Chase, Maryland. The pivotal moment came in 1909 when Scidmore wrote to First Lady Helen Herron Taft, who responded enthusiastically. This led to Japan's generous gift of 3,020 cherry trees in 1912. On March 27, 1912, First Lady Taft and Viscountess Chinda, wife of the Japanese ambassador, planted the first two trees on the Tidal Basin's north bank—a gesture that blossomed into the National Cherry Blossom Festival celebrated today. Here's a curated list of ten places to enjoy cherry blossom season in Washington, DC: Tidal Basin: A quintessential spot, the Tidal Basin is encircled by cherry trees, providing picturesque views of landmarks such as the Jefferson Memorial and the Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial. A leisurely stroll along the 2.1-mile path offers an immersive blossom experience. National Mall: Beyond its monuments and museums, the National Mall is adorned with cherry trees, especially near the Washington Monument, offering a blend of history and natural beauty. U.S. Capitol Grounds: The Capitol's west lawn features a variety of cherry trees, including Yoshino and Kwanzan species, set against the backdrop of the iconic Capitol dome. Kenilworth Park and Aquatic Gardens: A serene escape from the city's hustle, this park showcases cherry blossoms alongside aquatic flora, providing unique photo opportunities. Hains Point: Located in East Potomac Park, Hains Point is a tranquil spot where cherry trees line the waterfront, offering panoramic views of the Potomac River. East Potomac Park: Adjacent to the Tidal Basin, this park features numerous cherry trees along its pathways, ideal for walking, jogging, or cycling amidst the blossoms. Dumbarton Oaks: Nestled in Georgetown, the gardens of Dumbarton Oaks feature cherry trees amidst terraced landscapes, combining horticultural artistry with seasonal beauty. U.S. National Arboretum: Spanning 446 acres, the Arboretum boasts various cherry tree species, making it a botanical haven during the blooming season. Congressional Cemetery: An off-the-beaten-path location, this historic cemetery is adorned with cherry blossoms, offering a peaceful and reflective environment. Washington National Cathedral Grounds: The Cathedral's gardens and grounds are home to cherry trees that, when in bloom, enhance the site's architectural grandeur with natural elegance.
